name: Sixth Economic Census unit records and metadata
access: Public metadata; microdata registration and terms; download not obtained
social: SC ST OBC Others for eligible ownership
use: Best broad frame for informal mining; obtain original microdata to estimate within-district differences and employment distributions. Social group is identity, not a network. Verify ownership skip rules in schedule 6A.

name: Sixth Economic Census All India Report
access: Downloaded government-authored report from a third-party mirror
use: Actual empirical input. Tables 2.5 and 4.5 give state mining establishments and workers; Tables 12 and 15 give proprietary establishments and employment by owner group. Official landing page is https://www.mospi.gov.in/all-india-report-sixth-economic-census. The mirror is an acquisition route, not a new statistical producer.

name: Fifth Economic Census 2005
access: Metadata verified; unit data not acquired
growth: Area and group changes if definitions harmonized
use: Pair with EC6 at stable geographic and industry cells. Do not treat independent censuses as a firm panel. Harmonize NIC2004 and NIC2008, ownership coverage, reporting rules and geography. Retrieve final rather than provisional tables.

name: Fourth Economic Census and eSankhyiki dashboard
access: Public dashboard; export route to verify
use: Third cross-section can improve pre-trend context; a dashboard does not ensure a downloadable consistent panel. Preserve the release vintage and denominators.

name: Seventh Economic Census release status
access: Official FAQ says finalization underway
use: Do not assume an accessible final microdata release. The checked FAQ describes continuing finalization. Record the status on 10 October 2026; revisit before a dissertation data freeze.

name: Economic Census establishment directory
access: Public state directories
unit: Named establishments with at least ten workers
use: Potential fieldwork frame for larger units. The official note describes undercoverage and an employment threshold. It cannot represent small quarries alone; collect a supplemental area listing.

name: Maharashtra Sixth Economic Census report
access: Downloaded government report from NITI for States repository
growth: All-sector repeated counts, not mining firm growth
use: Actual input for district mining counts and employment, Tables 2.5 and 4.5. Matched to 2011 district boundaries; keep Thane before Palghar split and preserve historical district names.

name: State Economic Census reports and statistical offices
access: Public reports; state-specific archives vary
use: Expand district replication to Rajasthan, Odisha, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Gujarat, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh. State report families are candidates, not all downloaded. Seek custom caste by mining by district tabulations from DES.

name: Census 2011 Primary Census Abstract
access: Downloaded Excel workbook
use: Actual demographic input. SC/ST population share measures local composition; it is not the caste of entrepreneurs or a tie intensity. Literacy uses population age seven and above. No comparable universal OBC denominator is present here.

name: District Census Handbooks and village directories
access: Public tables and handbooks
use: Village infrastructure, accessibility, workforce structure and historical settlement context. Match mining coordinates to contemporaneous boundaries and calculate buffer-based measures only when resolution supports them.

name: PLFS and earlier NSS employment surveys
access: Public metadata; register for unit data
use: Estimate mining workers employment, wages and occupational segmentation using industry codes and survey weights. Workers social group does not identify employer caste. Inspect annual design changes and industry-code vintages before pooling.

name: India Human Development Survey
access: Public documentation; data via repository terms
social: Jati broad group religion social capital
use: A useful source for mechanisms and survey-question development; assess whether mining businesses have sufficient observations. Household nonfarm business income may combine activities and cannot automatically be assigned to a mining firm.

name: IHDS social group documentation
access: Public documentation
growth: No mining outcome on this page
use: Separate jati, broad social group and religion. The documentation offers coding guidance; do not treat its categories as interchangeable with the EC residual Others category.

name: IHDS income and social capital questionnaire
access: Public questionnaire
use: Adapt neutral name-generator questions and distinguish family, jati, religious community, business association and political access. It is a questionnaire source, not evidence about mining ties in the current analysis.

name: ASUSE and NSS unincorporated enterprise surveys
access: Public survey documentation and registered microdata
use: Excludes mining section B in the checked coverage. Can study eligible transport, repair, trade and other ancillary businesses with a mining exposure measure. Never label these records a mining operator sample.

name: Annual Survey of Industries
access: Public metadata; registered unit data
growth: Factory outcomes subject to identifier access
use: Downstream processing and eligible mineral-based manufacturing. Quarrying, mine operations and mineral manufacture have different coverage. Verify the factory frame and NIC before adding any plant.

name: Historical mining establishment follow-up survey 1992-93
access: Existence described in census history; archive not acquired
use: An obscure lead worth pursuing with MoSPI archives: the EC history identifies a mining and quarrying follow-up survey in 1992-93. No usable microdata, variables or complete report were located in this work; do not overstate availability.

name: Indian Bureau of Mines Indian Minerals Yearbook
access: Public volumes and commodity chapters
use: Mineral definitions, production, reserves, sector composition and state reviews. Coverage differs across fuels, atomic and minor minerals. Useful for geology and commodity-market confounders, with a mine-level availability audit.

name: IBM monthly mineral production statistics
access: Public monthly reports
use: Construct mineral-specific demand and output trends. Publication lag and revisions matter. A state-mineral series is contextual and does not reveal a particular firms growth.

name: IBM Mining Tenement System returns
access: Operational login; research access must be requested
unit: Mine holder monthly and annual returns
growth: Potential mine production employment sales panel
use: High-priority administrative request for deidentified mine identifiers and longitudinal quantities. The existence of a filing portal does not mean private returns are open. Request filing status and nonresponse flags with outcomes.

name: IBM registration plans notices and ratings
access: Public modules plus restricted sections
use: Link mine identifiers, operators and approval dates. Ratings are selected among reporting mines and are not exogenous treatments. Access and historical snapshots require verification.

name: IBM average sale prices
access: Public month and year series
use: Deflate sales using relevant mineral and grade. Revenue may rise while tonnage falls. These prices are not an automatic valid instrument for caste ties because they directly affect demand and profitability.

name: IBM mining lease bulletins and National Mineral Inventory
access: Public publications; detailed spatial access varies
use: Request vintage-consistent lease and resource measures. Geological endowment is crucial to regressions but is not a credible excluded instrument for caste networks because it directly affects mine growth.

name: Ministry of Mines annual reports and auction summaries
access: Public reports
use: Build a legal and auction timeline then verify the operative instrument for each event. The report alone cannot establish random assignment or a caste mechanism.

name: MSTC major mineral block auctions
access: Public notices; bidding logs restricted
use: Public tender and block summaries can define exposure. Full bids, participation, eligibility failures and unsuccessful bidders are essential for selection and close-auction analysis; availability is unverified.

name: MSTC minor mineral auctions
access: Public state auction notices; fuller data conditional
use: Important for small operators often missed in major-mineral records. State regimes vary. Separate auction award, permit approval, commencement and actual production dates.

name: Coal Directory of India
access: Public PDF and chapter Excel files
unit: Coal lignite mine company state year
use: A verified source family with downloadable chapter spreadsheets listed for 2024-25. Relevant for coal operators and procurement ecosystems, but PSU production does not reveal supplier-owner caste.

name: Coal monthly statistics
access: Public reports
use: Match dispatch and production cycles to supplier surveys and outcomes. Preserve fiscal-calendar mapping and distinguish mining from coal trading.

name: Directorate General of Mines Safety
access: Public annual reports; mine-level request needed
use: Triangulate mining coverage and incidents. Inspections are often targeted, so comparing inspected and uninspected mines is not a causal evaluation without an assignment design.

name: Directorate General of Hydrocarbons
access: Public outlook; repository terms vary
use: NIC mining includes hydrocarbons, but they require a separate institutional and data regime. Core small-quarry fieldwork should not be extrapolated to petroleum extraction.

name: PARIVESH environmental and forest clearances
access: Public project records and documents
use: Potential project-to-firm linkage and permit delay outcomes. Approved capacity is not observed production. Delays can reflect project risk and application quality, so approval timing is endogenous.

name: State Pollution Control Board consent records
access: Candidate state-board portals and requests
use: Follow the relevant board from project records and verify access to Consent to Establish and Consent to Operate. No unified national mine panel was acquired. Useful for entity validation and operating-status checks.

name: Odisha mining lessee register
access: Public lessee report verified
use: Columns include lessee code, area, IBM code, mine code, location and mineral. A strong starting point for fieldwork and linking returns to firms without inferring caste from names.

name: Odisha i3MS transaction system
access: Public descriptions and some MIS; transactions conditional
use: Administrative codes distinguish lessees and licensees. Seek deidentified production and dispatch histories and legal access to cross-firm transactions. A transporter, licensee and mine owner are different units.

name: Rajasthan mines and geology records
access: Candidate public directories and state requests
use: Priority fieldwork state for stone and other quarrying. Check Rajasthan-specific minor mineral rules and obtain a current operator frame; the source family was identified but no lease panel downloaded.

name: Other state mining and geology departments
access: Candidate state portals and administrative requests
use: Include Gujarat, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and Meghalaya. Inspect each departments source schema rather than presuming identical registries or public access.

name: MCA company and LLP master data
access: Public master-data portal verified
use: Link mine operators to legal firms. Registered office state may differ from mine location. Incorporation does not establish operations; current active status does not prove historical survival.

name: MCA company filings and research access
access: Research guidelines; filings may need account and payment
use: Build financial growth outcomes with standalone versus consolidated accounting clearly separated. Guidelines describe researcher access conditions; company-specific data access is not assumed here.

name: CMIE Prowess
access: Commercial institutional subscription
use: Practical dissertation option where the university has access. Inspect coverage of unlisted mining operators, exit treatment, identifier history and business groups. Company panels still require a consented network module.

name: NSE corporate annual reports and financial filings
access: Public filings
use: Cheap route for listed operators and parent groups. Provides a selected formal sample, not the quarry population. Ownership and director links measure corporate networks, not caste.

name: Company investor relations and PSU reports
access: Candidate firm and PSU websites
use: Collect mining-specific segment outcomes from relevant operators such as coal, metal and state mineral enterprises. The catalogue flags a source family; it does not claim all company reports were inspected.

name: Udyam registration and MSME dashboards
access: Public aggregates; restricted unit records
growth: Possible turnover employment histories by permission
use: A high-priority request for NIC mining by social group by district by year. Registration counts measure formalization as well as entry. Multi-activity enterprises and multiple plants complicate industry attribution.

name: Udyam registration instrument
access: Public application documentation
social: General SC ST OBC and ownership rules
growth: No outcomes on the form itself
use: Verified evidence that social category is recorded. Read entity ownership rules before assigning the entrepreneurs category to a multi-owner enterprise; administrative category is not a direct jati or tie measure.

name: National SC ST Hub and NSIC
access: Public scheme information; unit monitoring by request
use: Possible partner for an ethical network-brokerage trial or eligibility-based evaluation. Application, selection and take-up are endogenous unless randomized or a defensible cutoff exists.

name: CPPP procurement records
access: Public notices; awards and bids need audit
growth: Contract wins values and buyer links
use: Mine and PSU supplier networks, transport, overburden removal and equipment services. Request losing bids as well as awards; award-only data cannot estimate success probabilities.

name: GeM and PSU vendor registration
access: Candidate public portal; richer unit data conditional
social: Verified status may be available by agreement
use: Potential supply-chain outcome source. No GeM mining seller panel was obtained in this work. Avoid treating broad portal aggregates as a dataset of mining contracts.

name: RBI Database on Indian Economy
access: Public macro and banking series
use: Baseline financial access, state income and banking density. Aggregate credit does not reveal a firms loan access or who introduced the borrower.

name: GST EPFO ESIC banking and credit records
access: Restricted administrative sources; agreements required
use: Candidate research partnerships only, not downloaded data. Require authorized linkage and stable identities. No individual tax returns, payroll histories or credit reports were accessed.

name: DGCI and S trade data and port records
access: Candidate public aggregates and licensed details
use: Demand context for stone and mineral exports. Exporter-level availability and license terms need checking. Commodity HS codes must be crosswalked to NIC and mineral categories.

name: GSI Bhukosh and geological publications
access: Public catalogue; layer access varies
use: Geology is a central omitted variable in the completed regressions. Record resolution, survey vintage and uncertainty; do not equate mineral occurrence with commercially viable reserves.

name: District Mineral Foundations and PMKKKY records
access: Public district records; other districts to audit
use: Potential local-context and procurement sources. This verified district page describes project disclosure; no unified national panel was obtained. Spending assignment reflects mining revenues and need.

name: NCRB crimes against SC and ST
access: Public crime aggregates
use: Optional historical context. Recorded crime reflects reporting and enforcement; it is not a direct discrimination measure, and current crime must not be mechanically used as a pre-treatment control.

name: Remote sensing imagery and night lights
access: Candidate open satellite sources
use: Landsat, Sentinel and VIIRS can validate footprint changes or activity. Physical excavation is not firm profitability or employment; clouds, illegal activity and neighbouring plants complicate attribution. No imagery analysis was executed.

name: Mining associations cooperatives unions and district industry centres
access: Candidate institutional lists and interviews
use: Local associations can identify overlooked operators and contractors. Membership lists are selected. Do not use an association or chamber as the sole sampling frame, and do not infer individual caste from names.

name: Consent-based primary firm and relationship panel
access: To be collected through fieldwork
social: Self-reported identity and explicitly reported ties
use: The indispensable source for the actual research question. The URL is a questionnaire reference, not a dataset. Collect baseline, 12-month and 24-month outcomes and dated relationship histories; never fabricate respondents.

name: Census 2011 B18: all mining-industry workers
access: Downloaded official Excel; executed worker analysis
unit: Persons by industry, main/marginal duration, sex, residence, India and 35 historical states/UTs
social: All workers; join published SC/ST tables by exact codes
growth: One historical cross-section, no firm panel
use: Select division 05-09 with group 000 and class 0000 to avoid hierarchical double counting. Counts include workers beyond employees. Official duration definitions: https://data.gov.in/catalog/main-workers-marginal-workers-non-workers-and-those-marginal-workers-non-workers .

name: Census 2011 B18SC: SC mining workers
access: Downloaded official Excel; executed worker analysis
unit: SC persons by NIC division, sex, rural/urban and main/marginal status
social: Worker own SC identity, no jati or referral tie
use: Matched with all/ST tabulations. Preserve zero and absent division rows and workbook row numbers. Does not identify employer group.

name: Census 2011 B18ST: ST mining workers
access: Downloaded official Excel; executed worker analysis
unit: ST persons by NIC division, sex, residence and duration
social: Worker own ST identity, not a caste-network measure
use: Actual worker composition and duration baseline. Remaining = All minus SC minus ST includes OBC. Workforce shares do not measure access probabilities among the ST population.

name: Coal Ministry Annual Report 2023-24, welfare chapter 16
access: Downloaded official PDF; counts transcribed and reconciled
unit: Coal India employment groups A-D as on 1 January 2024
use: Full workforce composition table PDF page 5. Distinguish reservation quotas and PwBD tables from actual workforce shares; does not cover all Indian miners or all contractors.

name: Coal Ministry Annual Report 2025-26, welfare chapter 16
access: Downloaded official PDF; employee and selected recruitment tables used
unit: Coal India snapshot 1 January 2026; subsidiary advertised and filled vacancies
social: SC/ST/OBC/EWS in payroll; separate reserved/unreserved vacancy categories
growth: Two company stocks, no matched turnover or firm growth causal data
use: Workforce PDF page 4; SECL vacancy example page 7. Applicant denominators missing. UR vacancy category is not General worker caste. A separate SC/ST/OBC table concerns PwBD only and is not used as the full workforce numerator.

name: Arisa and CLRA: Caste in stone, November 2024
access: Downloaded and inspected primary producer report; selected aggregate facts retained
unit: 97 individual interviews in Budhpura/Makrana; local stone supply chain
social: Broad groups and published recruitment-route margins; no joint individual records
use: Composition pages 16/27; Makrana routes page 29. Non-probability local evidence. Ten Budhpura home-workers used a different instrument. Exact composition denominator unresolved; advance percentage discrepancy retained. Full publication is linked, not redistributed under the code licence.

name: ILO: Rajasthan natural stone productive employment and decent work, 2021
access: Downloaded and inspected primary ILO report; selected aggregates retained
unit: 115 workers and 43 owners in two local clusters; primarily formal value-chain respondents
social: Published SC/ST/OBC/General worker shares; qualitative job-entry routes
growth: No linked individual firm-worker growth panel
use: Methods page 18; profile page 55; work-year averages page 59. Rounded caste shares sum to 99; not normalized. No joint caste-route data acquired. Full publication is linked rather than redistributed.

name: PLFS 2023-24 first-visit/revisit layout and instructions
access: Downloaded layout Excel and instructions PDF; no unit records acquired
unit: Household social group and person-level labour survey records
social: Household sg; no employer caste or validated same-caste referral measure
growth: Labour outcomes and limited survey revisit design, not firm growth
use: Verified ind_pas/ind_sas, job_pas/job_sas, occupation, enterprise and earnings fields. Obtain unit records and exact survey design before controlled wage/formality analysis. Principal and subsidiary jobs and first/revisit records require explicit population definitions.

name: Labour Bureau Occupational Wage Survey, mining
access: Official survey description verified; specific seventh-round PDF identified, not downloaded
unit: Occupation-level wages/employment in selected mining industries
growth: Repeated industry wage context, not worker-firm panel
use: Specific report: https://labourbureau.gov.in/assets/images/pdf/OWS_7th_MINING_Jul_Dec_2016.pdf . Verify sample, occupation definitions and unit-data access; do not assume this gives caste-specific pay.

name: Labour Bureau SC/ST, unorganised and women-worker survey families
access: Candidate official archive; mining-specific release/schema not acquired
unit: Working/living conditions; industry and locality vary
social: SC/ST-specific survey family; jati/referral fields unknown
use: Search archives by coal, stone, quarrying, contractor and mineral; request schedules and mining subsamples. Survey-family availability does not establish a national modern mining-worker dataset.
